title: Can Large Language Models Capture Human Risk Preferences? A Cross-Cultural Study

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM-simulated decisions in lottery choice games to actual human survey responses using the Constant Relative Risk Aversion (CRRA) framework to detect systematic overestimation of conservative choices.

Evaluating the effect of linguistic framing by prompting the models in English versus Chinese for datasets from Hong Kong and Nanjing, and measuring the resulting deviations from real-world human risk preferences.
